in_text_mentions: after POEM. All patients with confirmed Barrett esophagus after POEM had concurrent reflux esophagitis during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. A flow chart of patients with suspected and confirmed Barrett esophagus is presented in Fig. 3 and endoscopy pictures of patients with Barrett esophagus are shown in Fig. 4. More characteristics and outcomes of patients with confirmed Barrett esophagus are provided in Supplementary Table S5. No cases of esophageal adenocarcinoma were observed in any of the patients during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy at a median follow-up of 100 months after POEM.

A: Panel A is H&E explicitly captioned as low-grade Barrett's dysplasia, showing dysplastic columnar epithelium of Barrett esophagus. B: Ki67 IHC of same low-grade Barrett's dysplasia tissue; gland architecture of dysplastic Barrett epithelium visible despite IHC stain. C: MUC2 IHC of low-grade Barrett's dysplasia glands; shows dysplastic Barrett epithelium. D: MUC5AC IHC of low-grade Barrett's dysplasia glands; shows dysplastic Barrett epithelium. E: TFF2 IHC of low-grade Barrett's dysplasia glands; shows dysplastic Barrett epithelium with preserved basal cells. F: MUC6 IHC of low-grade Barrett's dysplasia glands; shows dysplastic Barrett epithelium with preserved basal cells.

Figure 5 shows the distribution of Ki67+ cells, mucin core proteins and TFFs in low-grade Barrett's dysplasia (figure 5A H&E): the proliferative organisation mirrors that seen in Barrett's glands and, thus, in gastric glands, with preservation of the non-proliferative MUC6+/TFF2+ cells at the base of the gland. Figure 5B shows that the proliferative zone indicated by Ki67 expression expands towards the top of the glands, while the bases remain largely non-proliferative. panels.figure_caption: Endoscopic landmarks for determining the CLE. Endoscopic picture provided by Dr. PKD Phukan, General Surgeon. CLE: columnar lined epithelium.
in_text_mentions: unction between the pale pearly colored squamous epithelium and the salmon-colored columnar epithelium. The GEJ is usually identified as a pinch at the distal end of the esophagus, coinciding with the most proximal appearance of the gastric rugal folds. This point marks the beginning of the stomach and its distance from the Z line conventionally corresponds to the CLE [4,11]. Endoscopically the AZ distance/length of CLE can be measured by subtracting the distance of the incisor to the squamocolumnar junction (Z line) from the distance of the incisor to the gastroesophageal junction (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Top-left Type I raw ME-NBI image of Barrett lesion showing capillary/microvascular pattern. Disease attribution from disease-focused title on Barrett esophagus plus caption capillary pattern in lesion. Finding supported by caption microvessels/microvascular density. B: Top-right Type I image-processed ME-NBI with red vessel overlay and segmentation. Same Barrett lesion microvasculature as panel A, with image-analysis annotation. Still a real patient endoscopy image showing the manifestation. C: Bottom-left Type II raw ME-NBI image of Barrett lesion with dense microvascular network. Disease attribution from Barrett esophagus title plus captioned capillary pattern lesion. High-density vascular pattern supports irregular microvasculature finding. D: Bottom-right Type II image-processed ME-NBI with red vessel overlay and segmentation. Same Barrett lesion dense microvasculature as panel C, with annotation. Real patient endoscopy image...

panels.figure_caption: Representative images of microvascular density for each category of capillary pattern. Microvascular density was calculated by the percent area of microvessels in the lesion of interest by ME-NBI using image analysis software. The red line shows vessels selected from the image processed area based on a single-threshold level (hue, saturation, and luminance).
in_text_mentions: Vers. 1.5®, Olympus Medical Systems Co) as follows. First, the in-focus area was segmented from the full zoomed image of the lesion from which the biopsy sample was taken. Next, shading compensation to equalize the brightness of the image and differential contrast enhancement to enhance the contrast of the image were done for easy detection of microvessels in the segmented area. Then, the vessels were selected from the image-processed area based on a single-threshold level (hue, saturation, and luminance). Finally, the percentage of vessel area in the segmented area was calculated (Figure 4).
